growth_story.headline: Malawi's income per person grew fastest in 2007–2014, then stalled as scarce foreign exchange, droughts and rising debt took it back to its 2014 level.
growth_story.arc: Since 1990, Malawi's income per person has grown in four eras: 2.4 percent a year in 1990–1998, 0.0 in 1999–2006, 3.3 in 2007–2014 and 0.2 since 2015. The 1990s swung hard: income per person fell 10.0 percent in 1992 and 9.2 percent in 1994, then rose 16.9 percent in 1995. The World Bank describes a farm economy reliant on maize and tobacco and exposed to droughts, and multi-party rule from 1994 brought a strategy built on smallholder farming. Growth stalled from 1999 to 2006, with a fall of 7.2 percent in 2001, a badly handled 2001/02 food crisis and a suspension of donor budget support. The Growth Lab credits faster growth from 2006 to 2010 to debt relief, good weather and a jump in farm output after a farm input programme, though income per person fell 1.0 percent in 2012 as imports per person fell. Since 2015, earnings from tobacco and aid have stagnated, a fixed exchange rate ran down reserves, and deficits, debt and inflation have stayed high; income per person peaked in 2021, has fallen every year since, and in 2025 was 3.8 percent below that peak, about where it first was in 2014.

threads.title: Rain-fed maize and drought
threads.text: Much of Malawi's farming depends on rain-fed maize, which keeps rural incomes volatile. The World Bank tied this exposure to droughts in 2006, and the IMF links weak growth in 2024 to lower farm output and scarce foreign exchange.

threads.title: Aid cut-offs and weak governance
threads.text: Donors suspended budget support in 2001, 2010 and 2013, partly over corruption scandals. The 2001 suspension came in the flat 1999–2006 era, when the World Bank found the response to the 2001/02 food crisis badly handled. After the 2013 suspension, the World Bank says, public finances deteriorated rapidly.

threads.title: Debt relief and good weather
threads.text: The Growth Lab ties faster growth in 2006–2010 to debt relief, good weather and a jump in farm output after a farm input programme, a period when imports rose across the board. Income per person fell 1.0 percent in 2012 as imports per person declined, and the Growth Lab says imports have not returned to their earlier level since.

since_last_year.text: The IMF lending arrangement lapsed in May 2025 without a review, and a new government took office after the 2025 elections. In October 2026 the World Bank reported that the new government's tighter budget had started to narrow the deficit and that inflation began to ease in the first half of 2026. In June 2026 IMF staff opened talks on a new arrangement tied to the government's National Economic Recovery Plan.

growth_story.tension: The Growth Lab says income per person has been declining since 2020. The data show a fall of 1.8 percent in 2020, a rise of 1.9 percent in 2021 to the peak, and falls only from 2022. The World Bank also says growth strengthened in 2025, yet income per person still fell 0.7 percent that year because the population grew faster than output.
